public_rationale: The Decoder reported on February 27, 2026 that OpenAI's adjusted gross margin for 2025 was 33%, below its 46% target [e1]. This supports the claimed shortfall for the adjusted gross margin reported by that source [e1].
limitations: Support rests on secondary reporting, without the underlying investor presentation.
The evidence does not establish the margin definition, its reconciliation to other gross-margin measures, or the date and assumptions of the earlier target.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's gross margins in 2025 were worse than projected.

statement.excerpt: Anyway, The Information's piece also adds another fun detail - that OpenAI's margins were even worse than expected in 2025:
statement.document_title: News: OpenAI CFO Doesn't Believe Company Ready For IPO, Unsure Revenue Will Support Commitments

from_speaker: gross profit margins last year were lower than projected
our_interpretation: The surrounding quotation identifies the measure as gross profit margin and the comparison as OpenAI's own projection for 2025.
Treat 2025 as the full calendar year.

The claim concerns the company-defined margin communicated to investors. The accounting basis is company_reported because the context expressly attributes the figures to OpenAI's investor presentation, although the information reaches readers through reporting.
Any shortfall satisfies the claim; no minimum size is stated.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable reporting or company records show that OpenAI's realized full-year 2025 gross profit margin was below its earlier projection for that year.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show that OpenAI's realized full-year 2025 gross profit margin met or exceeded its earlier projection.
